messages:
leah: Heads up — seeing a weird loop after yesterday's RBAC changes. Users deprovision via SCIM but come back minutes later. Audit shows KMS decrypt failures mixed with SAML session renewals. Anyone seen this pattern?

devon: Hmm. Can you paste the relevant audit lines and the SCIM event payload?

leah: Pasting clipped logs:
```
2026-03-19T21:12:03Z audit: scim_service event=deprovision user_id=U12345 status=200
2026-03-19T21:12:04Z kms:Decrypt error key=alias/scim-key request=0xabc AccessDenied
2026-03-19T21:14:22Z auth: saml refresh user_id=U12345 assertion.SessionNotOnOrAfter=2026-03-19T21:20:00Z
2026-03-19T21:15:10Z audit: scim_service event=provision user_id=U12345 status=201
```
SCIM webhook payload (trimmed):
```
{ "id": "U12345", "action": "deactivate", "meta": { "source": "okta", "event": "post-deactivate" } }
```

ida: The KMS AccessDenied during the deprovision step is suspicious — if the scim_service can't decrypt the token used to call the user DB, it might abort cleanup and leave inconsistent state. But why a subsequent provision?

sre-oncall: Also note the SAML assertion TTL: SessionNotOnOrAfter gets extended via our IdP -> app relogin flow. If the app sees the user still active upstream it can trigger a reprovision. Could be race between deprovision attempt failing (due to KMS) and a background SAML refresh that re-syncs user.

devon: Do we have an ordered flow diagram? My hypothesis: 1) Okta sends deactivate, 2) scim_service tries to decrypt ephemeral token (KMS) to call user-db and fails, 3) scim retries or aborts leaving DB with stale active flag, 4) SAML/SSO probe from another service triggers a full user-sync which re-creates or reactivates the user.

leah: That matches timing. The deprovision log shows 200 then immediately a KMS error — weird ordering. I'm attaching the service's env snippet:
```
SCIM_SERVICE_ROLE=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-service
KMS_KEY_ALIAS=alias/scim-key
AWS_REGION=us-west-2
TOKEN_STORE_S3=s3://redwood-scim-tokens
```

ida: Can you run a quick check: confirm key policy allows scim-service role kms:Decrypt and that the alias points to the expected key id.

sam: Quick commands:
```
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/scim-key --policy-name default --region us-west-2
aws iam get-role --role-name scim-service
aws kms list-aliases --region us-west-2 | grep scim-key
```
I also recommend checking CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt failures around 21:12.

leah: Ran list-aliases and get-role — alias exists and role unchanged. Getting policy now. CloudTrail shows multiple kms:Decrypt AccessDenied entries from the scim-service principal in a 30s window.

devon: Two possibilities: key policy was accidentally narrowed in last RBAC change (removed scim-service from key policy) OR the scim-service assumed role ARN changed when we rolled out instance profile updates. Check the principal in the CloudTrail event vs the current role ARN.

leah: CloudTrail principal: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/scim-service/i-0a1b2c3d. Current role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-service. They line up.

ida: Did we recently enable KMS key grants with constraints? Grants can expire. Also check key rotation/alias re-pointing during last maintenance window.

sam: For immediate mitigation: create a temporary key grant for the scim-service:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-service --operations "Decrypt" --region us-west-2
```
If that clears the AccessDenied, we can roll back later and audit the key policy.

leah: Created a grant — SCIM deprovision now completes without KMS errors for the test user. No re-provision observed.

sre-oncall: Good. Root cause likely key policy/principal permission gap triggered by a timing window. Action items: 1) audit key policy and remove risky manual changes, 2) add CloudWatch alarm on kms:Decrypt AccessDenied spikes, 3) add an idempotent guard in SCIM to check for pending SAML refreshes before reactivating a user.

devon: Also recommend making the deprovision path durable: if KMS decrypt fails, enqueue a retry with backoff rather than partially succeed. And add a quick reconciliation job that checks recently deactivated users for reactivation signals.

leah: I'll open a follow-up ticket with the traces and the temp grant ID. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
